items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: We played, as you’d call them “eights” — challenges — eight bars for him, eight bars for me. And I’d play my eight bars, you know, and do my thing, and Basie would come up to his eight bars and he’d go like [brief scat] and wipe me out.

ctx.x: You can not hit it today. And so the idea was, Basie would look across at two pianos, and look at Oscar as if to say, “are you going to let me hit just one today? May I hit a key?” That was so, and you had to know the story.

He was beautiful. But you know he had a— he did so much with the piano in doing so little as many people think, but he did a lot. Because Basie could destroy you, whatever you’d play. We played, as you’d call them “eights” — challenges — eight bars for him, eight bars for me. And I’d play my eight bars, you know, and do my thing, and Basie would come up to his eight bars and he’d go like [brief scat] and wipe me out. You know, he had that ability, because his timing was impeccable. His choice of where to put what.
Did you know he used to be a drummer?

items.title: 52157_Count Basie oral history interview
items.q: I mean we did a couple things -- Pete and I did a couple things

ctx.x: To tell you the truth, I have kind of [pianist] different feelings altogether. We haven't really did anything together. I mean we did a couple things -- Pete and I did a couple things, but we just (inaudible), you know. But Tommy and I haven't been that close. And I love him, you know. Right in the number one slot as far as I'm concerned. As I said before, I think he's the most underrated pianist around.
